name: Adamantium
text: [what_to_bring] crampons — helped on the approach to the face

name: Beyer East Face I
text: [hazards] Early-season snowfield on the approach can be firm enough to need an axe;
[gear] Ice axe only if attempting early season, when a frozen snowfield can linger on the Teepe Glacier approach
[descent_text] Unrope, cross the snow-covered saddle about 50 ft wide, and zigzag up third- and fourth-class ground, avoiding snowfields, to the summit;

name: The Buck Sanction
text: [approach] Early in the season expect moderate snow climbing and wet rock on the lower route.

name: Cathedral Traverse
text: [overview] Ascend Owen by the East Ridge (5.6, possible snowfields) or the Koven Chimney (5.4);
[overview] Difficulty depends on snow and ice;

name: Chouinard-Frost Chimney
text: [overview] The full route begins in Glacier Gulch;

name: North Ridge
text: [overview] Past the second notch (snowy in cooler months), two pitches straight up lead to a moderate scramble.
[approach] Stay just right of the gully to avoid the worst brush, pass a cliff band, and climb the steep couloir of snow or talus to the ridge;
[approach] an ice axe and crampons are needed when it holds snow.

name: Crawl Along the Watchtower
text: [what_to_bring] footwear for snow — the walk to and from camp crosses the Teepe Glacier

name: Crystal Tower
text: [hazards] Steep, firm snow can guard the approach/base in early season, raising the consequence of a slip
[gear] Ice axe, and crampons if firm snow lingers near the base early season
[what_to_bring] ice axe — season may dictate carrying one.
[what_to_bring] crampons — perhaps, depending on season
[approach] this may cross steep firm snow depending on season and hour.

name: Dike route
text: [approach] Snow on the dike and the face can be scouted from there before committing.
[descent_text] Many parties do not go on to the summit at all: after the Dike Pinnacle they bail out by dropping into Garnet Canyon's south fork, or by heading north onto the Middle Teton Glacier.
[descent_text] The ground from the pinnacle to Ellingwood Col is convoluted and needs a rappel, and the col itself is a steep snow crossing of about 40 degrees that holds snow all year.

name: Direct Petzoldt Ridge
text: [hazards] Early-to-mid season snow on the ridge adds exposure and may require an axe.
[gear] Carry an ice axe if climbing early-to-mid season, when snow still lingers on the ridge.
[what_to_bring] ice axe — may be needed early or midway through the season
[approach] An ice axe may be needed in early to mid season.
[descent_text] with good snow the Ford Couloir is another way up.

name: East Face
text: [overview] Gain the bottom of it by continuing up the gully below the glacier and turning right.

name: Grasshopper Wall. West Face Left
text: [overview] The wall faces west above the Grasshopper valley, roughly 500 yards north of the glacier's toe, beside a huge chimney on its left.

name: West Face
text: [overview] P1: the lone significant break in the lower headwall leads, via a chimney of great cracks, to an overhang (snow and ice early in the year), then a crumbly low-angle slab to a slung block (5.6, 35m).
[approach] early in the season it is a tongue of snow and ice over a short overhang, later a chimney.
[descent_text] Then rappel to the snow or choss gully, downclimb it, and rappel to the base.

name: Koven Route
text: [overview] From Amphitheater Lake, go west down a ramp to the moraine by the Teton Glacier (tricky when snowy), cross the glacier end (melted out and/or unstable scree) and take the obvious couloir to the saddle just west of Teewinot;
[overview] Scramble west along the east ridge, then climb a cliff (easiest by a chimney to the right) to the upper snowfield and rise left to a spot south of the summit block.
[overview] Cliffs lie beneath the snowfield, so it is deceptively dangerous;
[overview] practice self-arrest or wait for melt-off.
[detailed_rack] add an axe for ice and, as the season dictates, normally crampons.

name: Lookin for Trouble
text: [detailed_rack] universal crampons and an axe, depending on the conditions.

name: Big Jobbin
text: [approach] It begins by ascending a snowfield to clean cracks in the middle right of the buttress.
[descent_text] The alternative is a series of double-rope rappels from the top of the fifth pitch down to the bottom of the snowfield.

name: North Face Highlight Tour
text: [hazards] Approach across the Teton Glacier is often a rock-fall horror show.
[hazards] Face holds snow/ice into summer;
[gear] Ice axe if climbing before August — the face holds snow and ice well into summer
[approach] The Valhalla Traverse from the Lower Saddle is the standard but takes at least three hours of loose, snowy and dirty traversing with tricky route-finding.
[approach] Up the Grandstand from the Teton Glacier is often subject to heavy rockfall.
[approach] The face holds snow and ice into summer, so August is best, and an ice axe is likely needed earlier.

name: North Ridge
text: [hazards] Overhead rockfall hazard on the glacier approach below the route.
[gear] Ice axe and crampons worth carrying for the Teton Glacier / Grandstand Direct approach depending on conditions
[approach] The Teton Glacier option (axe and crampons) adds glacier travel and route-finding;
[approach] Bivy spots include the Lower Saddle, the moraine below the Teton Glacier and near the top of the Grandstand.
